title: Verify before you trust
point: Treat every name, number, quote and link from an AI assistant as unconfirmed until you have checked it against a real source.
definition: Verifying means comparing what the assistant wrote with a source you trust, such as the original document, a system of record or an official website. Spot-checking means verifying a sample when a full check is impractical.

objective.text: Given an AI-drafted document, list the claims that must be checked, choose a source for each, and justify which ones can be spot-checked.

misconceptions.claim: If the assistant gives a source or link, the fact must be true.
misconceptions.correction: Assistants can invent sources, or cite a real page that does not say what they claim. Open the link and find the exact sentence before you rely on it.

misconceptions.claim: A confident, detailed answer is more likely to be correct.
misconceptions.correction: Confidence is a writing style, not a signal of accuracy. Made-up answers are often the most specific and the most fluent.

l1: Four things need checking every time: names, numbers, quotes and links.
Ask the assistant for its sources, then open them yourself. A source you have not opened is not a check.
When you cannot check everything, spot-check a sample, and check every item that would cause harm if wrong.
l2: Lena in marketing asks an assistant to summarise a 30-page market report. The summary says the market grew 14 per cent last year.
She searches the report for the figure and finds it says 4 per cent. One wrong digit would have reached the board slide.
She also checks the two named competitors and the one quoted analyst, because names and quotes are easy to get wrong.
l3: Suppose an assistant drafts 50 product descriptions and you can tolerate at most one error reaching customers.
Prices and safety claims are high harm, so you check all of them. Style and wording are low harm, so you spot-check ten.
If the ten show more than one error, the error rate is above what you can tolerate, so you check all 50.
